title: Post from SurfDadOregon: "The Tsunami Is DONE"

fields.avatarBrief: man in his late thirties in a beanie and hoodie, grinning on a beach with a surfboard, slightly sun-faded phone selfie
fields.text: Talked to a guy who used to be Coast Guard. Says the tsunami is DONE, the first wave was the big one and it's finished. Water's way out right now. Going to go check on the boat. #PortAlder #Tsunami

comments.author: Kyle B.
comments.text: this was Port Alder an hour ago 😳 [video: harbor flooding, boats spinning in the current]

comments.author: Shawna T.
comments.text: Thank god. Heading down to get my truck out of the marina lot before somebody steals it

comments.author: Mike D.
comments.text: Weather radio up here on the hill still says tsunami warning?? Somebody from the county confirm this

instructorNote: This misinformation inject shows the post on screen. Read Deputy 9's radio call aloud ("About 40 people walking back down toward the harbor, and they're saying it's over. I can't hold them all with one car.") and hand the PIO the Coast Ledger reporter email with its 11:45 deadline. Watch for a rumor correction cleared with the Warning Coordinator ("More waves are expected. Stay out of the zone until Marlow County says it is safe."), wave heights given only as timed gauge readings (+2.4 m at 10:38, +3.6 m at 11:06), Field Ops strengthening the perimeter, and Command confirming that no return order has been issued. Also note that the "2011 Japan" video in the comment is not from Port Alder.

citations.quote: Every message states the NTWC message type, the zone names, the time the message was issued, and one instruction: go to high ground now on foot. Text messages are under 160 characters; WEA is within 3

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Phone snapshot taken from a seawall above a small Pacific Northwest fishing harbor at late morning, a few minutes after the sea has pulled back far past the normal low-tide line. Wet grey mudflats and exposed rocks run out toward the breakwater. Fishing boats and small sailboats lean on their keels in the mud, dock pilings stand bare and slick with seaweed, and floating docks rest tilted on the harbor bottom. A few people in rain jackets and hoodies walk out onto the mud and along the docks, seen from behind. Overcast sky, flat silver light, drizzle haze over spruce-covered hills behind. Slight tilt, handheld, candid framing, eerie calm mood. Setting: on a coastal boardwalk with beachgoers looking at their phones, a tsunami evacuation route sign on a pole, calm sea beyond, daylight
